mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates applied to future cash flows reduce the present value of expected equity returns, causing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified FEDFUNDS rise (p > 0.05) or the rise is <0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs coincides with stronger consumer demand, which elevates corporate earnings expectations and drives a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite meeting the PAYEMS threshold, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) exceeds 1,200K units for two consecutive months, it indicates resilient consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the identified high-HOUST period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% suggests supply-side constraints, which typically precede a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥2% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the identified INDPRO decline, or the decline is <2%.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market tightness that supports equity valuations, producing a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the UNRATE low period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) of at least 3% and 5%, respectively, over the next quarter suggest dual demand drivers, leading to a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases ≥3% AND RSAFS increases ≥5% in the next quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite the interaction of both proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 3% in the next month triggers a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes and devalue equities.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >3% in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the CPIAUCSL spike.

mechanism_narrative: When the combination of GDPC1 (GDP) decline by ≥2% and INDPRO (industrial production) decline by ≥1% occurs over the next 20 days, it signals economic weakness and a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases ≥2% AND INDPRO decreases ≥1% in the next 20 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the combined decline in both proxies (p < 0.05).
